Anthropic’s assertion is only the latest move in a long-running debate about whether frontier AI models should be made open, like GLM-5.3, or should stay locked behind the doors of the frontier labs. These days, much of the debate about how to handle open models is playing out in public—and there’s a lot of money resting on its outcome. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, who has a lot to gain if people continue buying their own hardware to run open models, advocates enthusiastically for the United States to develop more of them, whereas Anthropic’s Dario Amodei, who runs a company that could be undermined by cheap, powerful models, advocates for a more cautious approach. But beneath all these commercial incentives, there is real substance to disagreements about open models. “I think a lot of the way you come down on the openness debate is influenced by how you come down on the AI debate,” says David Gray Widder, an assistant professor at the University of Texas at Austin School of Information. items.title: AI labs are buying data from dead startups to train their models
items.raw_text: When Keelan Miskell began winding down his crypto startup this year, he didn’t think its data was worth much: the users were anonymous, the company just a few years old. But he’s since turned the firm’s digital archives into real money. He’s netted roughly $25,000 for his code base and a still-pending amount (likely around $15,000) for the workspace data in Google, Notion, Figma, and Slack. “At least all that stuff we were doing for two and a half years is worth something to someone somewhere,” he says. The sale was brokered by a company called SimpleClosure, part of a new growth sector in tech: businesses catering to dying startups. Estimates from Carta and AngelList show shutdowns rising between 26% and 56% annually in recent years, and an end-of-life ecosystem—including coaches, “death doulas,” and firms that help handle the legal, tax, and operational headaches of going ­belly-up—has emerged. Now tech undertakers are selling the data remains to AI labs. SimpleClosure added data sales to its services in April. Its Asset Hub platform helps founders sell their code and workspace data—emails, chats, documents. Buyers include foundation AI labs, vendors that construct simulated workspaces for AI training, and mature tech companies building their own models. Asset Hub has handled over 150 deals and expects to return over $10 million to startups by the end of 2026. items.title: Metropolitan Libraries Spotlight: How Nanhai Library Is Reconnecting Children with the Classics
items.raw_text: When a thousand-year-old novel has to compete with a 15-second video In Foshan, in the heart of the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area, Nanhai Library serves a district of more than 3.7 million people, where local families, migrant workers, students, and seniors intertwine in a fast-moving, diverse community. It is also a community facing a very contemporary problem: as short-form video quietly absorbs every spare moment of screen time, deep reading is being pushed to the margins, even when the content at stake is centuries old. Rather than treat this as a lost cause, the library decided to meet children where their attention already lives. In April 2026, it launched Classics 101: Mental Models for Kids, a program built specifically for 10- to 12-year-olds — the exact age when children move from picture-to-text bridge books into more demanding reading. Making the classics legible again The challenge was concrete and specific. More than 60% of students in the first sessions admitted their biggest frustration was simple: they could not remember who everyone was or how all the characters connected. The semi-archaic language, sprawling character webs, and unhurried pacing of China’s Four Great Classical Novels were never designed to compete with instant gratification. So Nanhai Library stopped asking children to memorize plots and started extracting something more useful: practical mental models drawn directly from the characters’ journeys. items.title: The ecologist revealing the invisible networks that revive rainforests
items.raw_text: In a research station in central Panama, you can walk through a century of forest time, watching scrubby plots of adolescent trees give way to cathedral-­like canopies of mature growth. Forest ecologist Daisy Dent, a senior scientist at ETH Zurich, oversees this sequence of plots across the Barro Colorado Nature Monument, some of which date as far back as the 19th century. Not one of the trees she surveys was planted by human hands. She maps, measures, and tracks each trunk that emerges, revealing how waves of tree life rise from bare earth. Tropical forests like these are our planet’s biggest terrestrial carbon sink, accounting for around 40% of carbon stored on land . As part of an international network of researchers, Dent is deciphering the networks of animal and plant interactions that enable some forests to recover after destruction. The goal is a low-cost, high-impact alternative to typical carbon-­crediting schemes, which plant huge areas with a single species of tree. For over a decade, her research has built a body of evidence that such large “monocrop” programs could be expensive mistakes—and that more resilient forests can rebound naturally in just a few decades, re-creating ecosystems that suck up vast quantities of carbon dioxide. Few places are better to demonstrate this than Barro Colorado, a reserve covering the forested peninsulas and islands that formed when construction of the Panama Canal flooded the area in 1914. items.raw_text: De drastische besparingsplannen van de nieuwe Vlaamse regering slaan diepe wonden in de archief- en bibliotheeksector. Naast het nieuws dat landelijke erfgoedbibliotheken hun volledige structurele subsidies verliezen en archieven de helft moeten inleveren, luiden nu ook de informatieopleidingen en de sector voor passend lezen de noodklok. In twee brandbrieven waarschuwen de Arteveldehogeschool en Luisterpuntbibliotheek voor onomkeerbare schade aan het Vlaamse geheugen en de toegankelijkheid van informatie. Ook de VVBAD (Vlaamse Vereniging voor Bibliotheek, Archief & Documentatie ), Openbare Bibliotheek Brugge , Universiteitsbibliotheek Gent en Erfgoedbibliotheek Hendrik Conscience roepen op tot actie. Binnen het nieuwe begrotingsakkoord van minister van Cultuur Caroline Gennez moet de cultuur- en erfgoedsector vanaf 1 januari 2027 structureel 47 miljoen euro besparen. Voor de grote landelijke erfgoedbibliotheken – de Hendrik Conscience-erfgoedbibliotheek in Antwerpen, de Openbare Bibliotheek Brugge en de Gentse Boekentoren – betekent dit dat zij 100 procent van hun jaarlijkse Vlaamse subsidies kwijtspelen, een verlies van zo’n 1 miljoen euro. Erkende stadsarchieven en instellingen zoals het AMVB in Brussel zien hun middelen gehalveerd. items.raw_text: The fifth edition of the IFLA Futures Club offered an opportunity to explore what it looks like to apply futures thinking in libraries, in reality. Erik Boekesteijn and Cathelijne Kuiters of the Dutch National Library (KB) joined us to talk about their experience of running a concerted initiative to make futures thinking a more central part of the institution’s work, both with a view to shaping a new policy plan, and building skills more broadly. This was not the first time that futures had been on the agenda at the KB. Already, a ‘Club Stof’ had brought together colleagues throughout the sector, keen to get to grips with ‘the uncomfortable uncertainty of the future’. But with awareness that we are in a time where pre-existing ideas and assumptions are being challenged – epistemic turbulence – the Library’s new leadership was ready to take this work up a gear. There was an awareness from the start that this work provided an opportunity to think more broadly. First of all, an initaitive like this in the KB is not just an internal exercise, but also has potential impacts across the wider library field. National libraries usually have a kind of leadership within their fields, but the Dutch one has a formal role in supporting the country’s network of national libraries. Long-lost horror gaming cult classic P.T. gets a much-needed PC port
items.raw_text: For over a decade now, the only "official" way to play Hideo Kojima's cult classic, P.T. —the long-discontinued "playable trailer" for Kojima's canceled "Silent Hills" project —has been via one of the increasingly rare PlayStation 4s that previously downloaded a copy during its monthslong availability window. Now, though, one coder is helping to preserve the game with a porting tool that builds a playable x86 PC executable from the original PS4 files. Coder Lorean Xavier said he was inspired to work on the "P.T. for PC" project "because P.T. deserved to keep existing somewhere other than on consoles that still have it installed." The open source porting effort rebuilds the P.T. engine in C++ and Vulkan, using the original files from the PS4 game to re-create "every level, model, texture, sound, script and cutscene," according to its GitHub listing. That means players without their own legitimate decrypted copy of the original P.T. will have to track one down in order to generate a playable PC version. The reliance on real P.T. files makes this port more authentic than previous hobbyist efforts to re-create the look and feel of P.T. for a PC audience. And while PS4 emulators recently reached a point where they could run P.T. completely , this native port also sports extra features, like upscaling and frame-generation, a camera mode, experimental third-person and VR support, and a "museum" section where you can look at and listen to in-game assets (including "unused content").

The sport took to the floodlit streets of Singapore on Sunday night, but Saturday saw action, too; this Grand Prix weekend was also the final of six sprints this year. The night race might be one of modern F1’s greatest spectacles. From overhead shots, the track becomes a bright, illuminated ribbon among the looming darkness of the city-state’s overpasses and skyscrapers. At ground level, the cars shower glittering sparks from their titanium skid blocks as the drivers flirt with how close they can get to the walls. As tracks go, the 90-degree turns and concrete barrier-lined streets were a world away from the abrasive tarmac and ample runoff of Malaysia last time out . But the tropical heat and humidity were a constant given both locations’ proximity to the equator. On Saturday morning in Singapore, shortly before the start of the sprint, it seemed history was about to rhyme when the skies opened. items.raw_text: Google is releasing its second Fitbit tracker of 2026, offering fans of the aging Charge 6 a more refined option. The new Fitbit Edge slots right in between the Pixel Watch 5 and the Fitbit Air , featuring a compact screen and more health sensors than the Air. You won't get all the apps and features of the Pixel Watch 5, but the Edge is only about half as expensive. The Fitbit Edge is essentially a new Charge 6, but it has more of a Pixel Watch aesthetic. Squish Google's smartwatch from the sides, and you've got the Edge. It has a pill-shaped 1.34-inch OLED touch display inside a slender aluminum frame that is rated IP68 (5 ATM) for water and dust protection. Google says the screen has 46 percent more viewable area compared to the Charge 6. It's very close in overall size to the Fitbit Air and uses the same magnetic charging puck. Left to right: Fitbit Air (with new metal mesh band), Fitbit Edge, and Pixel Watch 5. Credit: Google The Edge works with Android or iPhones via the Google Health app, and it can run for about seven days on a charge. If the tracker is away from your phone, it can still follow your activity all week with support for seven days of full health data storage (or 30 days of basic data). However, the generous weeklong battery life does not include always-on display mode. If you turn it on, battery life drops to about two days, barely longer than the Pixel Watch 5. Teams die psychologische veiligheid inbouwen als fundamentele waarde kunnen fouten openlijk melden, herstellen sneller van incidenten en anticiperen direct op marktveranderingen. Beide sectoren verwerken gigantische hoeveelheden data onder extreme tijdsdruk, maar stuiten op dezelfde menselijke bottleneck. Marcia Goddard (Brain Matters) laat op EDAY volgende maand zien aan dat acute verandering en hoge werkdruk bij ontwikkelaars en analisten automatisch een biologische stressrespons activeren. Leiders omzeilen deze biologische blokkade door psychologische veiligheid in te richten als harde, neurologische fundering. Teams die fouten openlijk melden, herstellen direct van incidenten. Dit bouwt een structuur waarin medewerkers direct anticiperen op marktverschuivingen. Maar in de visie van ciso van de gemeente Den Haag, Lilian Knippenberg, blijft de beste verdediging een combinatie van mens en technologie. Dat blijkt uit haar terugblik op het jaarlijkse hackevenement van de hofstad, waar ethische hackers opnieuw tientallen kwetsbaarheden blootlegden in systemen van de gemeente en leveranciers. Hâck The Hague, dat 5 oktober 2026 plaatsvond, leverde 125 meldingen op. Het merendeel daarvan kon dezelfde dag nog worden opgelost. Volgens Knippenberg laat dat zien dat het evenement werkt als een versnellingskamer voor digitale veiligheid. items.title: DigiD-klokkenluider vraagt Europees Parlement om eID-bescherming
items.raw_text: DigiD-klokkenluider Pieter van Oordt heeft het Europees Parlement verzocht om de digitale soevereiniteit van eID-infrastructuur te waarborgen. De privacy-chef van DigiD-beheerder Logius, geschorst nadat hij naar buiten trad met zijn zorgen over DigiD, wil via een verzoekschrift een leemte in de Europese regelgeving dichten. Hij probeert via Brussel de infrastructuur van identificatiemiddelen zoals DigiD blijvend onder Europese zeggenschap te houden. Dat geeft de garantie dat DigiD ook op lange termijn buiten het bereik van de Amerikaans regering blijft. Het Witte Huis kan dan niet meer de stekker uit DigiD trekken waardoor bijvoorbeeld geen belastinginning meer mogelijk zou zijn. DigiD ligt volgens Van Oordt ‘niet in een veilige haven’, ondanks het feit dat het kabinet eind mei de overname verbood van het Amsterdamse Solvinity – het bedrijf achter het DigiD-platform – door het Amerikaanse Kyndryl. Risico’s voor het publieke belang waren de reden. De leverancier zou na de transactie onder Amerikaanse wetgeving met extraterritoriale werking vallen. Grip kwijtraken? De geschorste privacy-chef van Logius die als klokkenluider een ontslag boven het hoofd hangt, vindt dat een onaanvaardbaar gevaar. Maar de leiding van Logius ziet dat anders. Van Oordt stelt dat de digitale infrastructuur van DigiD, ook als Solvinity niet door Kyndryl wordt ingelijfd, kwetsbaar blijft voor mogelijke Amerikaanse invloeden.
